newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Ten die in Pakistan violence, faction vows fight.
newsitem.headline: Ten die in Pakistan violence, faction vows fight.

text.p: At least 10 people, including two ethnic activists and two Moslem militants, were killed in a surge of violence in Pakistan on Monday and Tuesday and a faction leader threatened to hit back.

Unidentified gunmen attacked the headquarters of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) in the southern port city of Karachi, killing two party workers, police said.
Haqiqi leader Afaq Ahmad blamed the government for the killings and told reporters that his faction would hit back.
"The evidence we have collected till now indicates direct involvement of the government or a government agency," he said.
"I have ordered my boys that if anyone attacks and kills one of our men they are free to kill 10 of those who had carried out the attack."
Karachi police chief Malik Mohammad Iqbal denied Ahmed's charge, saying it was premature to fix responsibility.
Two activists of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) Sunni Moslem group were killed on Tuesday night at Saray Saddu, near Multan in the central province of Punjab, police there said.
Haqiqi spokesman Younus Khan earlier said the gunmen attacked the faction's main office in Karachi's eastern Landhi district and killed Kashif Qayum, 18, and Naveed Ahmed, 21.
Haqiqi has long feuded with the mainstream MQM, which is now part of the coalition government in Sindh province.
Younus said the assailants came on foot and vanished in narrow streets after firing on the White House building. "The police were there, but did nothing to stop them," he said.
Elsewhere in Karachi, middle-aged Qari Abdul Ghafoor, prayer leader of a Sunni mosque, was kidnapped and later shot dead by unknown people, the police said.
The attack followed separate shooting in Karachi on Monday night in which five young people, including a 16-year-old girl, were killed by gunmen firing from a moving car.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility and it was not clear if the attack was politically motivated.
Witnesses said tension gripped the whole area after the shooting. Armed men took to the streets firing in the air.
More than 50 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
